justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Catalogue Microservice handles browse/search via Amazon OpenSearch; Checkout & Cart Microservice supports carts and secure transactions; Review & Rating Microservice covers 5-star reviews; Recommendation Microservice provides 'Customers also bought' suggestions; and Localization Service handles multi-currency.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance and scalability are explicitly tackled: CloudFront edge delivery, Lambda@Edge, OpenSearch indexing, Redis and DAX caching, PgBouncer pooling, and asynchronous messaging via Amazon SQS enable handling 1M MAU and achieving sub-2s page loads on 3G.
justifications.compatibility: External integration is well-defined: Checkout & Cart Microservice integrates with Payment Gateway and Third-Party Shipping APIs via Amazon SQS and REST/HTTPS. Multi-currency and regional needs are handled via Currency & Translation Resolver Component and Geo-Router Component.
justifications.usability: Shoppers and Vendors & Admins are cleanly served through tailored modules in the Single Page Application, backed by the Vendor Portal Microservice and Catalogue Browser. However, distinct interfaces or accessibility guidelines for varied end-user devices are minimally detailed.
justifications.reliability: A high 99.95% uptime target is supported via Multi-AZ PostgreSQL, DynamoDB Global Tables, Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) in Amazon SQS, circuit breakers in Notification Dispatcher Component, and fallback routines in Cache & Fallback Manager.
justifications.security: Addressed thoroughly: AWS WAF Rule Engine mitigates OWASP Top-10; Service Mesh Proxy enforces zero-trust mTLS; AWS Secrets Manager & KMS protect secrets/data at rest; PostgreSQL implements Row-Level Security (RLS); and MFA and tokenized payments ensure PCI/GDPR/CCPA alignment.
justifications.maintainability: Well-decomposed microservices architecture using ECS Fargate, decoupled by API Gateway & WAF, gRPC/mTLS, and Amazon SQS queues. Level 3 components show strong separation of concerns, such as dedicated controllers, orchestrators, and persistence wrappers.
justifications.portability: Targets AWS regions well through ECS Fargate, Lambda@Edge, and DynamoDB Global Tables. While Dockerized services and standard databases (PostgreSQL) facilitate migration, there is heavy coupling to proprietary AWS-native services like App Mesh, SQS, and Lambda@Edge.

PERF-01.justification: CloudFront CDN, OpenSearch, and containerized ECS services support horizontal scaling and caching for read-heavy catalogue traffic. However, strict 2-second budgets over 3G depend heavily on SPA bundle sizes and asset optimization.
sensitivity_points: CloudFront edge caching efficiency and hit ratios
OpenSearch query latency under high concurrent load
tradeoffs: Read replica cost versus catalogue query latency during traffic surges

PERF-02.justification: The recommendation microservice is isolated from catalogue browsing. Its internal Redis cache, Fallback Manager, and asynchronous architecture ensure continuous catalogue browsing performance even during batch scoring runs.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio in the Recommendation Microservice Redis layer
CPU isolation between offline scoring and real-time inference
tradeoffs: Serving stale recommendations to protect frontend response times

AVAIL-01.justification: The Checkout & Cart service publishes shipping dispatches asynchronously to Amazon SQS with Dead Letter Queues, completely decoupling checkout transactions from downstream shipping API downtime.
sensitivity_points: SQS queue retention and retry backoff policies for partner APIs
tradeoffs: Asynchronous fulfillment visibility traded against immediate checkout completion

AVAIL-02.justification: Although DynamoDB Global Tables provide multi-region support, core transactional order ledgers rely on RDS PostgreSQL configured only for Multi-AZ within a single region, lacking automated cross-region database failover without order loss.
sensitivity_points: RPO and RTO of cross-region PostgreSQL replication
Global DNS and edge traffic steering convergence speed
tradeoffs: Consistency in transactional databases traded against multi-region automated failover

MOD-01.justification: Currency handling is localized in the Lambda@Edge Currency & Translation Resolver and injected via custom headers. Changes are localized, though adjustments to payment gateway payloads and cart components are still required.
sensitivity_points: Standardized currency schema propagation across microservices
tradeoffs: Edge-based header translation simplicity versus backend conversion auditability

MOD-02.justification: The Recommendation Microservice cleanly encapsulates algorithm variants behind an Experiment Router and Scoring Engine. Standardized gRPC interfaces ensure changes remain entirely internal with zero blast radius.
sensitivity_points: Adherence to uniform contract interfaces between router and scoring engine
tradeoffs: Interface abstraction overhead versus flexibility in swapping algorithm implementations

SEC-01.justification: Inbound requests are inspected by AWS WAF Rule Engine and AWS Shield before reaching downstream services. Internal communication enforces mTLS via AWS App Mesh and parameterized database queries across services.
sensitivity_points: Regular updating of managed WAF rule sets against OWASP Top-10 vectors
tradeoffs: Inspection latency added by WAF rules versus injection protection depth

SEC-02.justification: The architecture lacks a centralized privacy coordinator or saga mechanism to propagate deletion requests across distributed datastores (PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, OpenSearch, S3 error logs) within statutory deadlines.
sensitivity_points: Traceability of PII across distributed relational and NoSQL databases
tradeoffs: Data deletion compliance complexity versus microservice datastore autonomy
